outgoing.name: 20th century
outgoing.excerpt: Vocals predominated in Hawaiian music until the 20th century, when instrumentation took a lead role.

outgoing.name: Dance
outgoing.excerpt: There are also religious chants called oli; when accompanied by dancing and drums, it is called mele hula pahu.

outgoing.name: Genealogy
outgoing.excerpt: Other chants are for specific purposes like naming, (mele inoa), prayer (mele pule), surfing (mele he'e nalu) and genealogical recitations (mele koihonua).

outgoing.name: Jamaica
outgoing.excerpt: Jawaiian is a Hawaiian style of reggae music, a genre that evolved in the late 1960s and early 70s in Jamaica.

outgoing.name: Tokyo
outgoing.excerpt: In 1929 they recorded eight songs in Tokyo, one of the first recordings of traditional Hawaiian music.

outgoing.name: English language
outgoing.excerpt: …at about the same time, traditional Hawaiian music with English lyrics became popular — this was called hapa haole.
